mainTopic: Hairs during the time (תוך זמן), the status of a girl past twelve for מיאון and חליצה, and the vows of a youngster near adulthood
overview: This amud asks about hairs that grow during the year just before the age of adulthood (תוך זמן). Do they count like hairs that grew before that age (לפני זמן), so they are not a sign? Or do they count like hairs after it (לאחר זמן)? רב המנונא and רבי זירא bring sources showing they count like before the time, and the גמרא calls this a תיובתא against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. רב נחמן tries to show that the question is a מחלוקת תנאים, using the first and last lines of a ברייתא. The גמרא answers that both lines can agree, and that they differ only about when a boy's or a girl's 'time' begins. רבא rules that תוך זמן כלפני זמן. The גמרא then works through רבא's rule that a girl past twelve does neither מיאון nor חליצה, and explains it using the חזקה that she has grown signs and the worry that her hairs fell out. Finally, רב הונא teaches that a youngster near adulthood who consecrates food and eats it gets מלקות, and a source in his support is introduced.

steps.title: The inference that ends רב המנונא's challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the source רב המנונא quoted: the hairs count only because they came after the time, so hairs during the time must count like before the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't the reason that the hairs count is that his development was completed after the time? That implies that if the hairs came during the time, it is as if they came before the time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge (from רב המנונא) that began just before this point. It points out that the source only counts hairs that appeared after the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source made the hairs count only once the age was reached. So the reason they count is the timing, 'after the time.' From this the גמרא infers the opposite case: hairs during the time do not count. They are treated like hairs before the time, which goes against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: During the time: the year leading up to the age of adulthood
Before the time: before the age when hairs can count as a sign
After the time: once the age of adulthood has been reached
His matter was completed: his physical development reached its full point

phrases.english: And the reason is that it is after the time
that his matter was completed for him?
phrases.notes: 'His matter' here means his growing up, meaning the signs of adulthood.

phrases.english: This implies that during the time is like before the time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דִּלְאַחַר זְמַן הוּא דְּגָמְרָה לַהּ לְמִילְּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב המנונא's objection from the previous part of the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי, who hold תוך זמן כלאחר זמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source makes the hairs count only because they came after the time. So hairs during the time must count like before the time.

steps.title: רבי זירא brings a ברייתא about vows
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא adds another challenge. He quotes a ברייתא saying that the word 'איש' includes a boy of thirteen years and a day, whose vows count even if he can't explain them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רבי זירא challenged: The פסוק says 'When a man shall clearly utter a vow.' Why does the פסוק say 'man'? To include someone who is thirteen years and one day old: even though he doesn't know how to explain his vow clearly, his vows stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא brings a second challenge against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. Here he only quotes the source; the next step will explain why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the extra word 'איש' that a thirteen-year-old's vows are valid, even without the usual check of whether he understands. The key detail is the age, thirteen years and one day. רבי זירא will use this detail in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? Points to a seemingly extra word
To include: an extra word teaches that an additional case is covered
To clearly express: to explain who the vow is for and what it means
His vows stand: they take full effect

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
"When a man shall clearly utter a vow"
Why does the verse say "man"?

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: To include one who is thirteen years and one day old,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְהַפְלִיא
phrases.english: that even though he does not know how to express it clearly
his vows stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection on top of רב המנונא's
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up a ברייתא whose age detail will imply that hairs during the time do not count

steps.title: Working out the ברייתא: it must mean he has two hairs
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא shows the ברייתא must be talking about a boy with שתי שערות. Since it stresses the age of thirteen and a day, hairs during the time must count like before the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is this? If he hasn't grown two hairs, he's a קטן! So it must mean he has grown two hairs. And the reason he counts as an 'איש' is that he is thirteen years and a day. This implies that hairs during the time count as if they came before the time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains why the ברייתא is a problem. It must be about a boy with two hairs, and it only calls him an adult because he has reached thirteen and a day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without hairs, a boy is a קטן at any age, so the ברייתא must assume he has hairs. Yet it still makes the age the deciding factor. That suggests hairs that came during the year before thirteen would not make him an 'איש'. This means תוך זמן כלפני זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What exact case is meant?
Two hairs: the physical sign of adulthood
A minor, who is not obligated in מצוות and whose vows do not take effect
Rather, isn't it…? Introduces the only remaining option

steps.confusionAlert: Age alone does not make someone an adult; he also needs שתי שערות. That is why the ברייתא must be talking about a boy who already has the hairs.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If he has not grown two hairs
he is a minor!
Rather, is it not where he has grown two hairs,

phrases.aramaic: וְטַעְמָא דְּבֶן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: and the reason is that he is thirteen years and one day old
that he is considered a "man",
which implies that during the time is like before the time!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא אַיְיתִי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא from step 2 to bring out the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי (תוך זמן כלאחר זמן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes the boy has hairs yet still depends on the age, so hairs during the time must not count.

steps.title: The challenge is declared a refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the challenge stands: it is a תיובתא against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that רבי זירא's challenge has no answer for now. The view that hairs during the time count like after the time seems disproven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means a clear source has contradicted an אמורא's opinion. But right away in the next step רב נחמן will push back, so this is not the last word.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a source has disproven an אמורא's view

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Declares that the challenge in step 3 succeeds
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי's view seems refuted by the ברייתא about vows.

steps.title: רב נחמן: this is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the question is a מחלוקת תנאים, and quotes a ברייתא about hairs at different ages. The next steps show where the dispute lies: the first line and the last line of this ברייתא imply opposite rules for the thirteenth year itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: This is like a dispute of תנאים. A nine-year-old who grew two hairs: it is a mole. From nine until twelve years and a day: it is a mole. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is a sign. At thirteen years and a day, everyone agrees it is a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי by saying תנאים argue about this question. Here he only quotes the ברייתא. The next steps show where the dispute is hidden in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hairs at age nine count as a שומא, hairs from a mole and not a real sign. From nine until twelve and a day the תנא קמא still calls them a שומא, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה calls them a סימן, and at thirteen and a day everyone agrees they are a סימן. רב נחמן's proof does not come from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It comes from how the first and last lines treat the thirteenth year itself, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the תנאים: the question is already a dispute between תנאים
A mole: hairs from a mole, not a sign of adulthood
A sign: a real sign of adulthood
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא cannot be refuted by one ברייתא if another תנא holds like him. רב נחמן tries to show such a תנא from this ברייתא, by contrasting its first and last lines (steps 6-7).
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a supposed refutation into a מחלוקת תנאים, so both views about hairs during the time stay possible.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is like a dispute of tannaim,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים שֶׁהֵבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת
phrases.english: a nine-year-old who grew two hairs
it is a mole,
phrases.notes: These hairs are treated as growing from a mole, so they don't show adulthood.

phrases.aramaic: מִבֶּן תֵּשַׁע וְעַד שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: from nine until twelve years and one day
it is a mole.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סִימָן.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: It is a sign.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: At thirteen years and one day
all agree it is a sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the תיובתא declared in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the issue is a מחלוקת תנאים, so the אמוראים can follow the other תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא about vows seemed to settle that hairs during the time count like before the time.
steps.terutzMaskana: That ברייתא about vows reflects one side only. Another ברייתא's first line treats the thirteenth year as after the time, and רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי can follow that line.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself about the thirteenth year
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן points out that the first line of the ברייתא implies hairs in the thirteenth year are a סימן, while the last line implies they are only a שומא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult. First you said: from nine until twelve years and a day, the hairs are just a mole. That means hairs in the thirteenth year itself are a real sign. Then it teaches: at thirteen years and a day, the hairs are a sign. That means hairs in the thirteenth year itself are just a mole!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן points out that the beginning and end of the ברייתא seem to say opposite things about hairs that grow during the thirteenth year. This sets up his next move, where he will explain the contradiction as two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line stops the 'mole' period before the thirteenth year begins, so the thirteenth year itself must count as a sign. The last line starts the 'sign' period only after thirteen full years, so the thirteenth year itself must still count as a mole. The same stretch of time cannot be both.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
A mole: hairs that grow from a mole and do not show adulthood
A sign: hairs that do show the child has reached adulthood
And then it teaches; used to bring the later line of the same source

steps.confusionAlert: 'Twelve years and one day' is the end point of the 'mole' period, so the thirteenth year itself falls outside it. 'Thirteen years and one day' is the start of the 'sign' period, so the thirteenth year itself falls before it. Read both lines this way and the contradiction becomes clear.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said: "From nine until

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד״ — שׁוּמָא,
phrases.english: twelve years and one day" — it is a mole,

phrases.aramaic: הָא שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה גּוּפָא — סִימָן,
phrases.english: which implies that in the thirteenth year itself — it is a sign,
and then it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד״ — סִימָן,
phrases.english: "Thirteen years and one day old" — it is a sign,

phrases.aramaic: הָא שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה גּוּפָא — שׁוּמָא!
phrases.english: which implies that in the thirteenth year itself — it is a mole!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן looks closely at the ברייתא he brought in step 5 to build his proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא about hairs in the thirteenth year
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The implication of the first line (the thirteenth year is a סימן) clashes with the implication of the last line (the thirteenth year is a שומא).

steps.title: So the two lines must be two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן concludes that the first line holds תוך זמן is like after the time and the last line holds it is like before the time, so this is a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it a dispute between תנאים? One Sage holds that 'during the time' is like 'after the time,' and the other Sage holds that 'during the time' is like 'before the time.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן resolves the contradiction by saying the two lines come from two different תנאים who disagree. This gives רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי a תנא to rely on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line treats the thirteenth year as 'after the time,' so hairs then count as a sign. The last line treats it as 'before the time,' so hairs then are only a mole. Because the question is a real dispute between תנאים, the earlier תיובתא no longer forces out רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it so that...? It introduces a suggested proof
It is a dispute between תנאים
During the time: the thirteenth year itself
Treated like after the time, so the hairs are a sign
Treated like before the time, so the hairs are a mole

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, the challenge from steps 1-4 does not knock out רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי. They simply follow one side of a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.english: What, is it not a dispute between תנאים?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר תּוֹךְ זְמַן כִּלְאַחַר זְמַן,
phrases.english: For one Sage holds: during the time is like after the time,
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of the first line, who makes the thirteenth year a sign.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר תּוֹךְ זְמַן כְּלִפְנֵי זְמַן?
phrases.english: and one Sage holds: during the time is like before the time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It resolves the contradiction from step 6 by giving the two lines to two different תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether תוך זמן counts like לפני זמן or like לאחר זמן is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The apparent contradiction between the first line and the last line of the ברייתא

steps.title: No: both lines are about a girl and follow different opinions about her age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Everyone holds תוך זמן is like לפני זמן. Both lines discuss a girl: the first line follows רבי and the last line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that 'during the time' is like 'before the time.' Both lines are talking about a girl. The first line follows רבי, and the last line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof. It explains the contradiction without any dispute about תוך זמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the תנאים agree that hairs during the time count like before the time. The real disagreement is about when a girl's 'time' arrives. For רבי, the thirteenth year is already after a girl's time, so hairs then are a sign. For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, it is still before her time, so hairs then are a mole.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
This one and that one: both lines
A young girl
The first line of a source
The last line of a source

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement here is not about the rule 'during the time is like before the time,' since everyone accepts that. It is about which year counts as the girl's 'time' in the first place.

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
that during the time is like before the time,
and both this and that are about a young girl,
and the first line follows רבי,
and the last line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא תּוֹךְ זְמַן כְּלִפְנֵי זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects step 7's claim that the ברייתא shows a dispute about תוך זמן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that תוך זמן is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction can be explained as a dispute about when a girl's 'time' begins, not about how to treat תוך זמן.

steps.title: Another option: both lines are about a boy, with the opinions reversed
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both lines discuss a boy. The first line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and the last line follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both lines are about a boy. The first line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the last line follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject רב נחמן's proof. This time both lines of the ברייתא are about a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone still agrees that תוך זמן is like לפני זמן. For a boy the two opinions flip. For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a boy's thirteenth year is already after his time, so hairs then are a sign. For רבי, it is still before his time, so hairs then are a mole.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
A young boy

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's proof that this is a מחלוקת תנאים is pushed aside. Both lines of the ברייתא can be read with everyone agreeing that תוך זמן is like לפני זמן. They differ only about when the child's 'time' begins: for a girl in one reading, and for a boy in the other, according to רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
both this and that are about a young boy,
and the first line follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר,
and the last line follows רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It offers a second way to reject step 7, reading the ברייתא as about a boy instead of a girl.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that תוך זמן is a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The contradiction can just as well be explained as a dispute about when a boy's 'time' begins.

steps.title: Both lines follow רבי: one is about a boy, one about a girl
steps.stepSummary: A third way to reject רב נחמן's proof. Both lines of the ברייתא follow רבי. One line is about a girl and the other is about a boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both lines follow רבי. This one is about a boy, and that one is about a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to read the ברייתא so it does not prove a מחלוקת תנאים. Both lines can follow רבי, because they talk about different children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, a girl and a boy reach adulthood at different ages. So 'the thirteenth year' is after the time for one of them and still inside the time for the other. Each line can treat תוך זמן as לפני זמן, and the two lines do not argue.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: the גמרא is offering another possible answer
This one and that one: both lines of the ברייתא
A young boy
A young girl

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
this one and that one are both רבי,
this one is about a boy,
that one is about a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative to steps 8 and 9 for rejecting רב נחמן's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two lines of the ברייתא are a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed both lines are about the same kind of child

steps.title: Both lines follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: one is about a boy, one about a girl
steps.stepSummary: A fourth way to reject the proof. Both lines follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Again, one is about a boy and one is about a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: both lines follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This one is about a boy, and that one is about a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer as before, this time using רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view of the ages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also gives a boy and a girl different ages of adulthood, but he flips which one comes first. So the boy-and-girl split works for his view too. The result is that the ברייתא can be read four ways, and none of them proves a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: There are four ways to read the ברייתא: girl/girl, boy/boy, all רבי, or all רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In every reading, everyone can hold תוך זמן כלפני זמן, so רב נחמן's proof does not stand.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: this one and that one are both רבי שמעון בן אלעזר,
this one is about a boy,
that one is about a girl.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 10, using the other תנא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two lines can be split between a boy and a girl according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר as well

steps.title: Early hairs count as a sign only if they are still there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says early hairs are a סימן. רבי כרוספדאי explains that this is only when the hairs are still present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is a sign. רבי כרוספדאי, son of רבי שבתאי, said: and this is only when the hairs are still on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier ברייתא and explains when רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה counts early hairs as a סימן of adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hairs that came between age nine and twelve could fall out. רבי כרוספדאי limits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view: the hairs count only if they are still there when the child reaches the age of adulthood. If they fell out, they were just a שומא (a mole).

keyTerms.meaning: A sign, here a sign that the child has become an adult
A mole: hair that does not count as a sign of adulthood
And this is only when they are still on him

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סִימָן.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is a sign.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שַׁבְּתַאי:
phrases.english: רבי כרוספדאי, son of רבי שבתאי, said:
And this is only when they are still on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 5 and limits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Early hairs count as a סימן for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only if they are still present

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי כרוספדאי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells out the case as hairs that are 'still on him.' This matches רבי כרוספדאי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught like this: A boy nine years and one day old who grew two hairs: it is a mole. From nine until twelve years and one day, and the hairs are still on him: it is a mole. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי כרוספדאי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, the case where רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees includes the words 'and they are still on him.' So he calls the hairs a סימן only when they stayed. That is exactly what רבי כרוספדאי said.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs: the basic physical sign of adulthood

phrases.english: It was also taught like this:
a boy nine years and one day old
who grew two hairs: it is a mole,

phrases.aramaic: מִבֶּן תֵּשַׁע וְעַד שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: from nine until twelve years and one day,
and they are still on him: it is a mole.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: סִימָן.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: it is a sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי כרוספדאי's explanation in step 12
steps.raayaObject: רבי כרוספדאי's rule that the hairs must still be present
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that includes the words וְעוֹדָן בּוֹ in the case under dispute

steps.title: רבא rules that hairs during the time count as before the time
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that hairs appearing in the year before adulthood count as if they came before the time. They do not make the child an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה is that 'within the time' is like 'before the time.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final הלכה on the main question of the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether hairs that appear during the year before adulthood count as a sign. רבא rules that they do not: תוך זמן is treated like לפני זמן. So these hairs are only a שומא.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה: the practical ruling
Within the time: the year right before the age of adulthood
Like before the time: hairs here do not count as a sign

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבא: תוך זמן כלפני זמן. Hairs during the year before adulthood do not make the child an adult.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Within the time' does not mean 'after reaching the age.' It means the year leading up to the age of adulthood.

phrases.english: רבא said: the halacha is:
within the time is like before the time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the main question that the earlier steps argued about
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Hairs during the year before adulthood are treated as if they came before the time, so they are only a שומא

steps.title: Another version of רבא's ruling, using the law of refusal
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר זוטרא reports רבא's ruling in different words. A minor girl can do מיאון all through her twelfth year. After that she does not do מיאון and does not do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר זוטרא taught רבא's teaching in this wording. רבא said: a minor girl, all through her twelfth year, can keep doing מיאון. From then on, she does not do מיאון and she does not do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how רבא's ruling was taught. This version uses the case of a girl's right of מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the same idea is stated as a practical case. Through the whole twelfth year the girl is still treated as a minor, even if hairs appeared, so she can still do מיאון. Once that year is over, she can no longer do מיאון, and she also does not do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Wording, version
A minor girl
Does מיאון: a minor girl's refusal that cancels a marriage set up by the Rabbis
Does חליצה with her late husband's brother

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבא's rule about תוך זמן has practical results, such as whether a girl can still cancel her marriage through מיאון.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
phrases.english: רב שמואל בר זוטרא teaches it,
this teaching of רבא, in this wording:
רבא said:
a minor girl, all through her twelfth year,
can keep on doing refusal,
phrases.notes: Refusal (מיאון) lets a young girl whose marriage was arranged by her mother or brothers walk away from it.

phrases.english: from here on,
she does not do refusal and she does not do חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא דְּרָבָא בְּהַאי לִישָּׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different wording of the same ruling of רבא from step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor girl can do מיאון all through her twelfth year. After that she does not do מיאון and does not do חליצה.

steps.title: רבא's ruling seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: If a girl past twelve cannot do מיאון, she is treated as an adult. Then she should be allowed to do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ruling itself is difficult. You said she cannot do מיאון, which shows she is an adult. If she is an adult, let her do חליצה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's ruling from Step 15. It says the two halves of the ruling do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a minor can do מיאון, and only an adult can do חליצה. If her inability to do מיאון means she is an adult, she should be able to do חליצה. Saying 'no' to both seems to treat her as neither a minor nor an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: This statement itself is difficult. The problem is inside the statement, not from an outside source.
Does מיאון. A minor girl married off by her mother or brothers refuses and leaves the marriage.
An adult woman
Let her do חליצה, the ceremony that frees a widow from יבום

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about whether she grew hairs. It points out that the two parts of רבא's ruling seem to be based on opposite assumptions about her status.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
You said 'she does not do מיאון,'
which shows she is an adult.
If she is an adult, let her do חליצה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of רבא's ruling as reported in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that after twelve a girl does neither מיאון nor חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not allowing מיאון implies she is an adult. Adults do חליצה, so forbidding חליצה contradicts the first half.

steps.title: רבא cannot simply be in doubt, since he trusts a חזקה
steps.stepSummary: One might answer that רבא is unsure of her status and is strict both ways. But רבא himself rules elsewhere that a girl of age is presumed to have grown signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say he is in doubt: is he really in doubt? Didn't רבא say that a minor girl who reached her years needs no checking, because we presume she grew signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a way out: רבא is unsure and is strict on both sides. It then knocks that suggestion down with another ruling of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבא were unsure whether she is an adult, being strict both ways would make sense. But רבא holds elsewhere that once a girl reaches age we assume she grew hairs, with no checking needed. So by his own rule she should be treated as an adult, and the question returns.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt
The full age of adulthood, twelve years and a day for a girl
An examination to see if signs grew
A legal presumption we rely on without checking
Signs of maturity: the two hairs

phrases.english: And if you will say he is in doubt,
phrases.notes: The idea is that רבא doesn't know if she is grown, so he is strict both ways.

phrases.english: But is he really in doubt?
But didn't רבא say:
A minor girl who reached her full years
does not need to be checked,
since there is a presumption she grew signs!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ, וּמִי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible defense to Step 16 and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבא is in doubt about her status
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself relies on a חזקה that a girl of age has grown signs, so he should not be in doubt.

steps.title: The חזקה applies only when she was not checked
steps.stepSummary: The חזקה applies to an ordinary case where nobody checked. Here they checked and found no hairs, so the חזקה does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies to an ordinary case. But here, where they checked and did not find, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge. It limits רבא's חזקה to cases where no one examined the girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה fills in when we have no information. Once they examined her and found no hairs, we cannot simply assume she has them. So רבא's ruling about no מיאון and no חליצה is about a girl who was checked, and there real doubt makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... (a limiting formula)
In an ordinary, unspecified case where nothing was checked
They checked and did not find

phrases.english: That applies in an ordinary case,
phrases.notes: The presumption from רבא's other ruling is meant for when no one looked.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דִּבְדַקוּ וְלָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ — לָא.
phrases.english: but here, where they checked and did not find, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 by limiting the חזקה to unchecked cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: רבא's ruling refers to a girl who was examined and found without hairs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The presumption that a girl of age grew signs applies to every girl past twelve.
steps.terutzMaskana: The presumption applies only when she was not checked. Once she was checked and no hairs were found, her status is unclear.

steps.title: If no hairs were found, she should be a minor
steps.stepSummary: If she was checked and has no hairs, she should be a full minor and be allowed to do מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let her do מיאון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If the check showed no hairs, why not treat her as a minor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 18 seems to prove too much. A girl checked with no hairs looks like a plain minor, and minors can do מיאון. So the 'no מיאון' half of רבא's ruling is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, according to your answer
Let her do מיאון

phrases.english: If so, let her do מיאון!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that she was checked and found without hairs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she has no hairs, she is a minor, and a minor can do מיאון.

steps.title: Maybe the hairs fell out
steps.stepSummary: We worry she had hairs that fell out, so she is in doubt. She cannot do מיאון like a minor or חליצה like an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are concerned that perhaps they fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: finding no hairs now does not prove she never had them. This answer is challenged in steps 21-23, and step 24 gives a different explanation of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is past twelve, so she may have grown hairs that later fell out. Finding nothing makes us unsure; it does not make her a definite minor. Because her status is doubtful, she is treated strictly both ways, and that explains רבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned, so we take a possibility into account
They fell out

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, the גמרא explains רבא's ruling as being about a girl who was checked and had no hairs. Because the hairs may have fallen out, she cannot do מיאון or חליצה. Step 24 later reads רבא differently.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how one ruling can be strict in both directions. The חזקה is pushed aside by an actual check, and the check is weakened by the possibility that hairs fell out.

phrases.english: We are concerned that perhaps they fell out.
phrases.notes: They means the two hairs. She may have grown them before the check, and they dropped off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 and fully explains רבא's ruling from Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A doubt that requires being strict both ways
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No hairs found means she is a definite minor and can do מיאון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hairs may have fallen out, so she is in doubt. She cannot do מיאון or חליצה.

steps.title: What about the opinion that does not worry the hairs fell out?
steps.stepSummary: The previous answer only works for those who worry that hairs fell out. רב פפא holds we do not worry, so how would he explain רבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says we worry the hairs fell out. But what can we say for the one who says we do not worry? This is a real argument: רב פפא says we do not worry that they fell out, and רב פפי says we do worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 20, because it depends on an opinion that not everyone holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 explained רבא by saying we worry the hairs fell out. But רב פפא and רב פפי argue about exactly this worry. According to רב פפא, a girl who was checked and had no hairs is simply a minor, so she should be able to do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one view, but what about the other?)
We are concerned / we worry
We are not concerned
Perhaps they (the hairs) fell out

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says "we are concerned,"
but according to the one who says "we are not concerned,"
what is there to say?
As it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא נָשְׁרוּ,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: we are not concerned that perhaps they fell out;
phrases.notes: "They" means the hairs, the signs that she is an adult.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi says: we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חוֹשְׁשִׁין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20 because it depends on a disputed opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבא's case is a girl who was checked, and we worry her hairs fell out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב פפא does not worry that hairs fell out. For him a checked girl with no hairs is a full minor and should be able to do מיאון, so רבא's ruling would not fit.

steps.title: Even רב פפא worries about hair falling out when it comes to מיאון
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא only does not worry when it comes to חליצה. For מיאון, everyone worries.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is only about חליצה. But about מיאון, we do worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא's lenient view is limited to חליצה, so for מיאון everyone agrees we worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא says we do not use the worry about fallen hairs to treat her as an adult for חליצה. But to block her from doing מיאון, even he worries. So רבא's ruling that she cannot do מיאון fits everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to... (limits a ruling)
With regard to
The ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her husband's brother
Refusal: a girl married off as a minor cancels the marriage

phrases.english: This applies only with regard to חליצה,
but with regard to מיאון, we are concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן חֲלִיצָה, אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן מֵיאוּן חוֹשְׁשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a disputed opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא never worries about fallen hairs, so a checked girl could do מיאון.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב פפא's 'not concerned' is only about חליצה. For מיאון all agree we worry, so she cannot do מיאון.

steps.title: Does the one who worries really allow חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The answer implies that רב פפי would allow חליצה. But he only has a doubt, and a doubt is not enough to make her an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that the one who says 'we are concerned' lets her do חליצה? But he only said 'we are concerned', just a worry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 22 by showing that it leads to a conclusion that cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is only about חליצה, then רב פפי, who worries, must let her do חליצה. But worrying only creates a doubt. A girl who is only possibly an adult cannot do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: By inference / this implies
She performs חליצה
Merely / just

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפי's 'we are concerned' does not mean we are sure she is an adult. It only means there is a doubt, and that is why it cannot be enough for חליצה.

phrases.english: By inference, according to the one who says "we are concerned," she performs חליצה?
But he merely says "we are concerned"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limitation offered in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the argument between רב פפא and רב פפי is only about חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Then רב פפי would allow חליצה, but a mere worry only makes a doubt, and doubt cannot make her an adult for חליצה.

steps.title: New explanation: she was never checked
steps.stepSummary: רבא is speaking about a girl who was not checked. His חזקה is enough to stop מיאון, but חליצה requires a real check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is really where they did not check her. For חליצה we worry she may still be a minor. When רבא said there is a חזקה, he meant for מיאון. But for חליצה she needs to be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the idea that she was checked and gives a new way to read רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was never checked, so we only have the חזקה that a girl of twelve has grown signs. A חזקה is strong enough to stop her from doing מיאון. It is not strong enough to let her do חליצה, which needs an actual check. This also answers the question from step 17 about רבא contradicting himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces the true case)
We are concerned
A presumption based on the usual situation
An examination / check

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's girl was not checked. The חזקה that she is an adult stops מיאון, but חליצה needs a real check. So she can do neither.

phrases.english: Rather, it is really where they did not examine (her) [them],
phrases.notes: Some versions say "examine her" (round brackets), but the corrected wording in square brackets is "examine them," meaning the signs.

phrases.english: and with regard to חליצה we are concerned,
and when Rava said "there is a presumption," it was for מיאון,
but for חליצה she requires an examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 23 knocks down the 'checked' approach, this redefines רבא's case as unchecked.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case and splitting the חזקה by purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's case was a checked girl with no hairs, and we worry they fell out (steps 18-20).
steps.terutzMaskana: She was not checked. The חזקה is enough to block מיאון, but חליצה needs a real check.

steps.title: The הלכה: we worry the hairs fell out
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי of נהרדעא rules like רב פפי: we worry the hairs may have fallen out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי of נהרדעא said: The הלכה is that we worry the hairs may have fallen out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the argument between רב פפא and רב פפי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows רב פפי. So even if a twelve-year-old girl was checked and no hairs were found, we still worry she had them. She therefore cannot do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical הלכה is

steps.whatToRemember: Practical ruling: חוששין שמא נשרו. We worry the hairs fell out, so a checked girl past twelve still cannot do מיאון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides the practical case: a girl past twelve with no visible signs is treated as possibly an adult and loses the right to מיאון.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Neharde'a said:
The halakha is: we are concerned that perhaps they fell out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument quoted in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב פפי: we worry the hairs fell out.

steps.title: The worry about fallen hairs applies only when Torah law may be involved
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי's worry that the hairs fell out applies only when he betrothed her before twelve and lived with her after twelve. That case raises a possible Torah-level marriage. If he lived with her only before twelve, there is no worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies only when he betrothed her during the time and lived with her after the time, because then there is a doubt about Torah law. But if he lived with her at the start, there is no such worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts a limit on the ruling from Step 25. It tells us exactly when we must worry that the girl's hairs fell out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband lived with her after she turned twelve, she might already have been an adult then. That would make the marriage a Torah-level marriage, so it is a real Torah doubt and we must be strict. If everything happened before twelve, the marriage is only from the רבנן, so there is no reason to be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: During the time, meaning before she reached twelve years and a day
After the time, meaning once she is twelve years and a day or older
A doubt about a Torah-level law, where we must be strict
At the start, meaning he lived with her only before she turned twelve

steps.whatToRemember: We worry that the hairs fell out only when there is a possible Torah-level marriage. That means betrothal before twelve and living together after twelve.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit of the ruling like רב פפי. The worry is not automatic. It applies only where Torah law might be at stake.

phrases.english: And this applies only where
phrases.notes: "This" is רב דימי's ruling from the last step, that we worry the hairs fell out.

phrases.english: he betrothed her during the time,
and lived with her after the time,
since there is a doubt about Torah law,
but at the start, no.
phrases.notes: If he lived with her only before she turned twelve, there is no worry at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of רב דימי in Step 25 to cases with a possible Torah-level marriage
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The worry that hairs fell out applies only when there is a Torah-level doubt: betrothal before twelve and living together after twelve.

steps.title: A young person who consecrates food and then eats it gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a young person in the year before adulthood who consecrated food and then ate it receives מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If he consecrated food and then ate it, he gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא teaches that a youngster on the edge of adulthood who makes food holy and then eats it is punished with lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a child is not punished. But in the year just before adulthood, a youngster who understands his vow can make real vows. רב הונא goes further: such a vow is real enough that breaking it brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated, meaning he made the item holy
He receives lashes (מלקות) as a Torah punishment

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא is not talking about any child. The context is a youngster in the year right before adulthood, whose vows already count.

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
If he consecrated and ate, he is flogged.
phrases.notes: The case is a youngster in the year before adulthood, as in the discussion around this part of the daf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הִקְדִּישׁ וְאָכַל לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the vows of a youngster near adulthood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A youngster near adulthood whose vow counts and who eats food he consecrated receives מלקות.

steps.title: רב הונא's source links real vows to the ban on breaking one's word
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא puts two פסוקים side by side. Whoever counts for making a clear vow (הפלאה) is also bound by בל יחל, the ban on breaking one's word. Whoever does not count for one does not count for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it says: "A man who clearly utters a vow," and "He shall not break his word." Anyone who counts for clear vowing is bound by "do not break," and anyone who does not count for clear vowing is not bound by "do not break."
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the Torah source for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that a youngster who clearly understands his vow can make a valid vow. The second פסוק forbids breaking a vow, and breaking it is punished with lashes. רב הונא ties them together: if your vow counts, then the ban on breaking it applies to you too, lashes included.

keyTerms.meaning: Clearly utters a vow, said with full understanding
Clear, understood vowing, which makes a vow valid
The prohibition "do not break your word" (not keeping a vow)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's principle: if someone counts for הפלאה, he counts for בל יחל. If his vow is valid, breaking it is punishable.

phrases.english: As it says: "A man who clearly utters a vow,"
and "He shall not break his word,"
anyone who is included in clear vowing
is included in "do not break,"
and anyone who is not included in clear vowing
is not included in "do not break."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק-based source for רב הונא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a youngster near adulthood gets lashes for eating food he consecrated
steps.raayaSupportSource: The link between במדבר 6:2 (הפלאה) and במדבר 30:3 (בל יחל)

steps.title: Setting up a source that supports רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה brings a challenge, but its purpose is to support רב הונא's ruling. The source itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה raised an objection (to רבא) in support of רב הונא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces that a source is coming to back up רב הונא; the actual source appears in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for "objection" is normally used to attack a view. Here the challenge is aimed at someone else (in some versions, רבא), and it ends up supporting רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: To support, meaning to bring backing for a view
An objection raised whose real purpose is to support someone's view

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רב הונא is being attacked. The verb sounds like an objection, but the line says outright that it is meant to support him.

phrases.english: רב הונא בר יהודה raised an objection
(to רבא)
